titulo: Last Person on Earth: 5 Movie Myths That Would Get You Killed
premisa: Movies vs Reality, 5 myths about being the last person on Earth, narrated in second person. The structure is myth, then reality, instead of a time countdown. Myth 1: 'You'd have free electricity forever.' Reality: most of the grid goes dark within hours to days with no one running the plants; only dams like Hoover could keep producing longer. Myth 2: 'You'd drive any Ferrari you want.' Reality: gasoline goes stale in roughly 6 to 12 months, so you end up on a bicycle. Myth 3: 'Supermarkets are endless food.' Reality: fresh food rots in weeks; canned food lasts for years, and honey basically never spoils. Myth 4: 'Cities would look like the movie, intact.' Reality: New York's subway pumps remove about 13 million gallons of water a day, and without them the tunnels could flood in about 36 hours. Myth 5: 'The real danger is wild animals.' Reality: the worst threat is loneliness; studies link chronic social isolation to health risks comparable to smoking 15 cigarettes a day. Finally, the twist.
gancho: What if you were the last person on Earth? Hollywood got almost everything wrong. Here are 5 myths that would get you killed.
